import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler, StandardScaler, RobustScaler, PowerTransformer
from scipy.stats import skew

# Complex dataset requiring multiple normalization strategies
np.random.seed(42)
data = {
    'age': np.random.randint(18, 70, 100),
    'income': np.random.lognormal(10, 0.8, 100),
    'score': np.random.normal(75, 15, 100),
    'rating': np.random.uniform(1, 5, 100),
    'transactions': np.random.poisson(10, 100).astype(float)
}
# Add outliers
data['income'][5] = 500000
data['score'][10] = -50

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Profile the dataset
print("=== Dataset Profile ===")
for col in df.columns:
    print(f"{col}: skew={skew(df[col]):.3f}, range=[{df[col].min():.1f}, {df[col].max():.1f}]")

# Apply appropriate scaling to each column
# PowerTransformer for highly skewed columns (income, transactions)
pt = PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson')
df[['income', 'transactions']] = pt.fit_transform(df[['income', 'transactions']])

# RobustScaler for age (has some outliers)
df[['age']] = RobustScaler().fit_transform(df[['age']])

# StandardScaler for approximately normal column (score)
df[['score']] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(df[['score']])

# MinMaxScaler for bounded column (rating)
df[['rating']] = MinMaxScaler().fit_transform(df[['rating']])

# Print summary
print("\n=== Transformation Summary ===")
print("income, transactions: Yeo-Johnson Power Transform")
print("age: RobustScaler")
print("score: StandardScaler")
print("rating: MinMaxScaler")
print("\nNormalized Data (first 5 rows):")
print(df.head())
print("\nPost-transform skewness:")
for col in df.columns:
    print(f"  {col}: {skew(df[col]):.3f}")
